_comment: Club members. archetype -> archetypes{} (tag dot / dialogue colours, tips). Small talk (MissionSystem + SmallTalk.js): the first chat of the day uses 'greetings'; later chats mix dialoguePool.idle, time lines (morning < 11:30 <= afternoon < 16:30 <= evening), weather lines (sunny / cloudy / rainy / windy) and, after a mission reaction, the mood lines (satisfied / neutral / unsatisfied). bio, quirks, voice, relationships, preferredTime and tennis are character notes (tennis.skill 0..1 also drives MatchSystem rallies). matchLines win/lose are post-match speech bubbles (keep them short). Hand-authored looks live in NPC_STYLES (src/entities/NPC.js).

npcs.name: Mrs. Wellington
npcs.bio: Third-generation member whose grandfather paid for the original clubhouse, and she brings it up about once a week.
quirks: Calls every staff member 'the attendant'
Times service with a gold wristwatch
Keeps a monogrammed towel folded exactly in thirds
npcs.voice: Clipped, formal, never uses contractions when annoyed; rhetorical questions; 'In my day...'

tennis.style: Steady slice-and-lob doubles player who wins on patience

theo_wellington.note: Her grandson. She wants him at etiquette lunch; he wants a junior title.

diane_ross.note: Two former club presidents who disagree about everything, especially the other.

frank_deluca.note: Her ally on the bylaws committee. They agree that standards are slipping.

greetings: Finally! I've been waiting forever.
You there! Attendant!
I shouldn't have to ask twice.
Ah. The attendant. Walk with me, I have notes.
Good morning. It is still morning, is it not? One loses track waiting.
requests: My usual court isn't ready. This is unacceptable.
Bring me fresh towels immediately.
Someone left balls all over Court 1. Clean it up.

satisfied: Hmph. I suppose that'll do.
About time.
Adequate. I shall mention you favourably. Briefly.
unsatisfied: I'll be speaking to the manager about this.
Unbelievable.
My grandfather built that clubhouse for better than this.
neutral: Fine. It is done, I suppose.
Neither here nor there. Carry on.
idle: The service here used to be much better.
Is that what passes for court maintenance?
Diane Ross wore white sneakers to the gala. Sneakers.
My grandson Theo is at etiquette lunch. At least, he had better be.
Frank and I have drafted a proposal about proper tennis attire. You will be enforcing it.
In my day, one applauded a good shot. Now they all just shout.
That Chad boy called me 'dude'. I have not recovered.
morning: The morning light is the only civilized time to play.
I take my tea at nine sharp. You may note that.
afternoon: The afternoon crowd is so... enthusiastic.
Luncheon on the patio was lukewarm again.
evening: I do not care for the floodlights. Tennis is a daytime sport.
Is it that late? Someone should have told me.
rainy: Rain. And not a single umbrella offered. Remarkable.
Wet clay is a crime against the game.
windy: This wind has ruined a perfectly good lob.
Hold onto your visor, dear. I've lost two this season.
cloudy: Overcast. At least one doesn't squint.
The clouds suit my mood.
sunny: Splendid weather. Wasted on most of them.
Do fetch me the shaded table if it opens up.

npcs.name: Chad Blake
npcs.bio: Former high-school #1 singles player who still introduces himself that way; his dad sits on the club board.
quirks: Breaks a string every week and blames the string
Films his own serve on his phone
Wears his cap backwards, always
npcs.voice: Bro-speak, ALL-CAPS emphasis, repeats words for effect, sentence fragments, big claims.

tennis.style: Big first serve, bigger mouth; falls apart in long rallies

nate_okafor.note: Can't stand that Nate is better and doesn't brag about it.

tommy_chen.note: Hitting partner. Tommy is the only one who laughs at his jokes.

jess_nakamura.note: His best customer and her biggest headache.

otis_grant.note: The security guy. Chad thinks they're buddies. Otis thinks about radar guns.

greetings: Bro, bro, BRO.
Hey! Cart boy!
Yo, I need something.
My guy! Did you see that serve? You didn't? Unreal.
Heyyy, the legend. Kind of. Not as much as me.
requests: Someone took my reserved court. Handle it.
I need a ball hopper at Court 2, like NOW.
My racket got scuffed. The pro shop better have a replacement.

satisfied: Solid. Respect.
That's what I'm talking about.
You're like, my favorite employee. Top three.
unsatisfied: Weak. Seriously weak.
My dad's gonna hear about this.
Not cool, bro. Not cool at ALL.
idle: Check out this serve. Watch. WATCH.
I could've gone pro, you know.
Nate Okafor thinks he's so good. He IS good. That's what's annoying.
Jess says I'm 'statistically her worst customer'. Is that a compliment?
Tommy grunts louder than me now. I gotta step it up.
Broke another string. Third one this week. Strings are just weak now.
Hit 118 on the radar gun once. Okay, 97. Still.
morning: Too early, bro. My serve's still asleep.
Protein shake. Then tennis. Then protein shake.
afternoon: Peak serve hours right now. Science.
Grinding. Always grinding.
evening: Under the lights, baby. Main character hours.
Nate and me, tonight, Court 1. Tell everyone.
rainy: Rain delay?! I was just getting warm!
Bro, my shoes are suede. SUEDE.
windy: Wind's totally why I shanked that. Totally.
This wind is doing my toss dirty.
cloudy: Clouds are good. No glare for the serve cam.
Kinda gloomy. Good thing I'm here.
sunny: Perfect tanning weather. And tennis. Mostly tanning.
Sun's out, serves out.

npcs.name: Maria Santos
npcs.bio: Pediatric nurse on her days off, chairs the garden committee and brings her daughter Lily to every junior clinic.
quirks: Carries sunscreen for everyone
Names the fountain koi
Knows everyone's kids' birthdays
npcs.voice: Warm, exclamation marks, lots of 'oh!', asks after you before herself.

tennis.style: Cheerful doubles volleyer who apologises for her winners

lily_santos.note: Her daughter, age ten. Boundless energy, boundless questions.

babs_hendricks.note: Garden committee co-chair. Maria plants, Babs talks.

priya_sharma.note: Took Priya under her wing on her first day.

greetings: Oh hi there! Beautiful day, isn't it?
Hey! How's your shift going?
Good to see you!
Oh, perfect timing! Have you had water today? Have some water.
Hi, sweetie! Have you seen a small girl with a very big racket?
requests: Would you mind checking if Court 3 is free at 3pm?
Could you bring some water bottles to the patio when you get a chance?
I think I left my visor at Court 4. Could you check?

satisfied: You're the best! Here, take this.
Thank you so much!
Oh, you're an angel. Lily, say thank you!
unsatisfied: Oh no worries, I'll figure it out!
That's okay, thanks for trying!
Oh, well, tomorrow's another day!
idle: The garden looks lovely today.
I just love this club.
Lily has decided she's going to beat Theo Wellington by summer's end. He's fourteen.
The koi in the fountain are named Serena, Venus and Gerald. Don't ask about Gerald.
Babs told me something about the flower committee I'm not supposed to repeat. So I won't! Mostly.
Priya's getting so much better. Did you see her backhand? Okay, it went over the fence, but still!
Tommy taught Lily to grunt when she hits. I'm choosing to find it adorable.
morning: Morning! I have already done three rounds of sunscreen on other people's kids.
The roses open up so nicely in the morning.
afternoon: Lunch on the patio? The fruit salad is actually fresh today!
Afternoon clinic is Lily's favorite.
evening: Look at that sunset over the courts. Worth every membership dollar.
Time to round up Lily. Wish me luck!
rainy: Rain's good for the garden at least!
Everyone inside! Lily, that means you!
windy: Hold on to your hat! Oh, there goes mine.
The windchimes on the patio are going wild!
cloudy: A little overcast is perfect for the hydrangeas.
Nice and cool. Good day to play long!
sunny: Don't forget sunscreen! I have extra!
Gorgeous out. The whole garden is showing off.

npcs.name: Bob Hendricks
npcs.bio: Retired high-school shop teacher, member for 38 years, tells the same five stories and they're all good.
quirks: Calls everyone 'kiddo'
Keeps butterscotch candies in his pocket
Still uses a racket he restrung himself in 1994
npcs.voice: Folksy, dad jokes, laughs at his own punchlines, 'back in my day', long pauses.

tennis.style: Moonball specialist; wins by making you lose patience

babs_hendricks.note: Married 41 years. She talks, he nods, both are happy.

gloria_castellano.note: Mixed doubles partner in the 1982 club championship. They lost. He still brings it up.

frank_deluca.note: Coffee buddy. Bob thinks the bylaws are 'more like guidelines'.

vik_rao.note: His knee surgeon. Bob shows everyone the scar, whether they ask or not.

gus_papadakis.note: Gus knows his order. Gus also knows not to tell Babs about the second hot dog.

greetings: Hey kiddo! How goes it?
There's my favorite attendant!
Good morning! Or is it afternoon? Ha!
Well if it isn't the hardest-working kid on the grounds. Butterscotch?
Hey hey! Pull up a chair. Oh, you're working. Right, right.
requests: Any chance you could grab me a cold drink from the pro shop?
My doubles partner hasn't shown up. Know anyone looking for a game?
Could you check the schedule for me? My eyes aren't what they used to be.

satisfied: You're a gem. Here's a little something for ya.
Fantastic, thanks a million!
Kiddo, you're going places. Probably the pro shop, but still!
unsatisfied: Ah well, no big deal!
Don't worry about it at all.
Eh, happens to the best of us. Happened to me in '82.
neutral: Good enough for government work! Ha!
idle: Back in my day, we didn't have fancy clay courts...
Gorgeous weather for tennis.
Gloria and I made the '82 club final. Lost 6-4 in the third. I was robbed! Well. I double-faulted.
Babs says I talk too much. Then she talks for an hour. Ha!
Frank read me bylaw 12 today. Took twenty minutes. There are forty bylaws.
You know why tennis players never get married? Because love means nothing! ...Babs didn't laugh either.
That Nate kid hits the ball harder than my old truck.
morning: Early bird gets the court, kiddo.
Coffee, a butterscotch, and a moonball. Perfect morning.
afternoon: Time for my afternoon rest. I call it 'watching tennis'.
Babs is at the committee. I'm hiding here.
evening: Look at those lights come on. Never gets old.
One more set, then home for Babs' pot roast.
rainy: Rain rain, go away, Bob wants to play. Ha!
Good day for a card game in the clubhouse.
windy: Wind's perfect for my moonball. It comes down in the next county!
Hang onto your hat, kiddo.
cloudy: Bit gray. Good for old eyes.
No sun, no squinting. I'll take it.
sunny: Sun's out! Where'd I put my hat? Oh. I'm bald. Ha!
Beautiful day, kiddo. Enjoy it.

npcs.name: Kevin Park
npcs.bio: Software engineer who joined because his startup's offsite was here; has watched 40 hours of tennis tutorials and played about two.
quirks: Apologises to the ball when he mishits
Keeps a spreadsheet of his serves
Wore running shorts on day one and Frank noticed
npcs.voice: Hesitant, trailing off with '...', over-apologetic, tech jargon when nervous.

tennis.style: Textbook form from YouTube, no idea where the ball will go

priya_sharma.note: They joined the same week and compare notes on the unwritten rules.

frank_deluca.note: Frank has cited him under the dress code three times. Kevin is terrified.

jess_nakamura.note: She sold him his first racket and quietly keeps him from buying the wrong grip.

otis_grant.note: Unlocked his car three times. Kevin sends him a thank-you card every time.

greetings: Excuse me, um, hi...
Hey, sorry to bother you...
Is this... am I in the right place?
Oh! Hi! Is it okay if I stand here? Is standing allowed?
Hey... quick question, is Frank around? No reason.
requests: Where exactly are the courts? I can't find them.
Do I need to sign in somewhere? I'm new.
My membership card isn't working at the gate. Can you help?

satisfied: Oh awesome, thank you! This place is so confusing.
You're a lifesaver!
That's... that's so helpful. Adding you to my notes. As a positive.
unsatisfied: Oh... okay. I'll just... wander around I guess.
Sorry, was that a dumb question?
No, totally, my bad. Bug on my end.
idle: This club is way bigger than I expected.
Everyone seems to know each other here...
Frank said my socks were 'a statement'. I don't think that was good?
Priya and I made a shared doc of club rules. It's 14 pages. Nobody told us any of them.
Jess told me my grip was upside down. How is that even possible?
I tracked my serves. 11% in. That's up from 4%! Trending!
Is 'love' zero? Why is love zero? Nobody will explain this to me.
morning: I'm usually still in standup at this hour...
Morning people here are very... intense.
afternoon: Took a long lunch to be here. Don't tell my team.
Afternoon is good. Fewer witnesses.
evening: Is it okay to play under the lights? Do they cost extra?
I should log off. I mean, go home.
rainy: Does rain cancel everything? Is there an app for that?
I didn't bring an umbrella. I didn't bring anything.
windy: The wind took my toss... and my hat... and my confidence.
Is wind a valid excuse? Asking for me.
cloudy: Cloudy is nice. I don't have to find my sunglasses.
Good lighting for not being seen.
sunny: I think I'm sunburned. Already.
Is sunscreen a dress-code thing?

npcs.name: Priya Sharma
npcs.bio: Architect who picked up tennis this spring on a dare; takes lessons from Coach Rafa and draws the courts in her sketchbook.
quirks: Sketches the clubhouse from every angle
Counts her steps between points
Brings the wrong ball type, every time
npcs.voice: Curious, lots of questions, self-deprecating, 'Sorry, one more thing...'

tennis.style: Great footwork, no idea what to do once she gets there

kevin_park.note: Fellow new member. They are figuring it out together, slowly.

rafa_ibarra.note: Her coach. She's learning to love his aphorisms.

gloria_castellano.note: Gloria adopted her after watching one lesson. Nobody knows why.

maria_santos.note: The first person here to say hi to her.

greetings: Hi! Quick question...
Hey there, I'm a bit lost...
Sorry, one more thing...
Oh good, a staff person! Is this the good clay or the other clay?
Hi! Don't look at my shoes. Gloria already said something.
requests: Which courts are clay and which are hard? Does it matter?
I signed up for a lesson but I don't know where to go.
Is there a dress code? Someone gave me a weird look.

satisfied: Oh that makes sense! Thank you!
Great, I feel so much better now.
Okay, writing that down. You're very good at explaining things.
unsatisfied: Oh no... I hope I didn't mess anything up.
This is all so overwhelming.
Right. Okay. I'll... figure it out.
idle: I should probably actually learn the rules of tennis...
The garden here is so peaceful.
Coach Rafa said 'the ball has no memory'. I've been thinking about it for three days.
Gloria told me I have 'the feet of a champion and the hands of a toddler'. Progress!
Kevin and I are writing a guide for new members. Chapter one: nobody tells you anything.
The clubhouse roofline is gorgeous. Very 1920s Colonial Revival. Sorry, architect brain.
Is a 'let' good or bad? I've been celebrating them.
morning: Morning lesson with Rafa! Or is it Thursday? It's Thursday, right?
The light on the clay in the morning is so pretty.
afternoon: I'm sketching the pro shop. Don't tell Jess, she'll make me buy something.
Afternoon practice. Wish my backhand luck.
evening: The floodlights make everything look like a stage set.
One more bucket of serves, then home.
rainy: Can you play in the rain? Should I? I'm asking the wrong person, aren't I.
My sketchbook is soaked. Worth it.
windy: Is the ball supposed to curve like that?
The wind blew my score card into the fountain.
cloudy: Soft light. Good for sketching.
A bit gray. Good day to practice without an audience.
sunny: It's so bright! Where do people put their sunglasses when they play?
Beautiful out. I'm going to draw the fountain.

npcs.name: Diane Ross
npcs.bio: Club president for six terms, deposed by a single vote, and she has the name of every voter in a notebook.
quirks: Carries a small leather notebook of grievances
Never removes her sunglasses
Refers to herself as 'a founding voice'
npcs.voice: Imperious, precise, rhetorical 'Excuse me?', short declaratives, numbers and dates as weapons.

tennis.style: Relentless moonballer who questions every line call

mrs_wellington.note: Thirty years of tennis-club cold war.

babs_hendricks.note: The flower committee feud: Diane wants roses, Babs wants hydrangeas.

chad_blake.note: Took his patio table. Would do it again.

tommy_chen.note: Four noise complaints filed. He waves every time. She hates the waving.

greetings: Excuse me. EXCUSE me.
I've been a member here for 15 years.
Where is the attendant? Oh, there you are.
Ah. You. Stand still, I'm writing something down.
I have three complaints. Four, now that I see your shoelaces.
requests: The patio umbrella is at the wrong angle. Fix it.
Those people on Court 4 are being entirely too loud.
I need the court swept before my 4 o'clock match.

satisfied: Acceptable.
See? Was that so hard?
Noted. In the good column, for once.
unsatisfied: This club is going downhill.
I'm writing a letter to the board.
That's going in the notebook.
idle: When I was club president, things were different.
The new members have no etiquette.
Babs Hendricks planted hydrangeas in MY rose bed. Hydrangeas.
Mrs. Wellington thinks she runs this club. She runs a book club. Badly.
I lost the last election by one vote. I know whose vote.
That young man Chad called me 'ma'am'. Twice. I'm keeping count.
Six terms as president. Six.
morning: I don't do mornings. I do complaints about mornings.
Coffee. Black. Like my notebook.
afternoon: Four o'clock is MY court time. Everyone knows this.
The afternoon crowd is a disgrace to tennis whites.
evening: The lights on Court 4 flicker. I've mentioned it. Twice.
Finally, the children have gone home.
rainy: Of course it's raining. I have a match.
I'll expect the courts dried by the time this stops.
windy: This wind has opinions. So do I.
My notebook nearly blew away. The board should be grateful it didn't.
cloudy: Gray skies. Fitting.
Overcast. I prefer it. Fewer people.
sunny: Sun's out, and so are the amateurs.
I'll need the shaded table. Now, please.

npcs.name: Tommy Chen
npcs.bio: High-school PE teacher on summer break who plays five hours a day and grunts like a pro on every shot.
quirks: Grunts on every shot, including warm-up
High-fives strangers
Teaches every kid at the club a trick shot
npcs.voice: Upbeat, sports clichés, 'my friend', laughs mid-sentence, zero sarcasm.

tennis.style: Topspin forehand machine; loud about it

chad_blake.note: Hitting partner. Tommy thinks Chad is a good guy underneath. Way underneath.

lily_santos.note: Taught her the tweener and the grunt. Maria has feelings about both.

diane_ross.note: She has filed four noise complaints about him. He waves every time.

greetings: Hey! Great to see you!
What's good, my friend?
Perfect timing!
Up top! Come on, don't leave me hanging!
My friend! You look like someone who needs a high-five.
requests: Got any extra balls? I'm hitting serves and running out fast.
My water bottle is in the cart. Could you grab it for me?
Want to rally for a bit when you're on break? Ha, just kidding. Unless...

satisfied: You rock! Seriously.
Here, grab yourself a snack on me.
MVP! Most Valuable Person-who-works-here!
unsatisfied: All good, no stress!
Haha, don't worry about it!
Next time, my friend. Next time.
neutral: Hey, it's all part of the game!
idle: Just trying to nail my backhand.
Tennis is therapy, am I right?
Taught Lily the tweener. Maria gave me a look. Worth it.
Diane says I grunt 'like a walrus in distress'. I'm taking it as a compliment.
Chad's actually a good dude. Deep, deep down.
Five hours on court today! My legs are jelly! Best day ever!
Nate hit a ball so hard it went through the net. Okay, it went over. But FAST.
morning: Rise and grind! Or rise and rally!
First hit of the day is always the best.
afternoon: Afternoon session number three, let's GO!
Hydrate or die-drate, my friend.
evening: Night tennis! It's like tennis, but at night!
One more bucket, then tacos.
rainy: Rain dance! No? Just me? Okay.
Rain's just nature's rest day.
windy: Wind's a great teacher. Keeps you humble!
Topspin cuts right through this wind. Watch!
cloudy: Cloudy's underrated. No sunburn, all tennis!
Great day to play forever.
sunny: Sunshine and forehands, baby!
What a day! What a DAY!

npcs.name: Hank Morris
npcs.bio: Grounds manager for 22 years; treats the clay courts like a vineyard and the new attendant like a promising apprentice.
quirks: Talks to the clay
Drinks thermos coffee at dawn with Gloria
Knows the moisture level of every court by smell
npcs.voice: Gruff, practical, farming metaphors, short sentences, dry praise.

tennis.style: Doesn't play. 'I build the stage, I don't dance on it.'

rafa_ibarra.note: Friendly running argument about how much water clay needs.

gloria_castellano.note: Dawn coffee on the Court 5 bench, every day for ten years.

frank_deluca.note: Frank reports every divot. Personally. In writing.

gus_papadakis.note: Morning coffee at the hatch for thirty years. Good coffee. Hank said so once.

otis_grant.note: Opens the gate while Hank opens the shed. They agree about the geese.

greetings: Morning! Those clay courts won't groom themselves.
Hey there! How are the courts looking today?
Good to see ya. Ready to put in some work?
There's my apprentice. Clay's thirsty today. Can you feel it?
Ah, good. Grab a rake and a good attitude.
requests: The clay courts are looking rough after the morning matches. Time for a sweep.
All three clay courts need attention before the afternoon lesson.
Those courts need grooming. Grab the brush from the equipment shed.

satisfied: Now THAT's how you groom a court. Well done!
Beautiful work. The members will love it.
Clay's smiling. I can tell.
unsatisfied: Hmm, you might want another pass on that. A few spots are still rough.
Not bad for a rookie, but we can do better.
Clay remembers sloppy work. So do I.
idle: A well-maintained court is a happy court.
Nothing beats the smell of fresh Har-Tru in the morning.
Rafa wants the clay wetter. Rafa is wrong. Don't tell him I said that. Tell him.
Frank handed me a memo about a divot on Court 4. Hand-written. Two pages.
Gloria and I have coffee on the Court 5 bench at six. Every day. Ten years.
You brush the lines last, kid. Always last.
Chad slid into the net post again. The post's fine. Chad's fine. Mostly the post.
morning: Dew's still on the clay. Best time to read a court.
Early start. Clay likes an early start.
afternoon: Afternoon heat dries the clay fast. Keep an eye on it.
Busy courts, tired clay.
evening: Courts get a rest at night. So should you. After closing.
Lights on. Last sweep before lock-up.
rainy: Rain's the clay's best friend and my worst enemy.
No grooming in this. We wait it out.
windy: Wind's lifting the top dressing. Keep that brush low.
Windy days, the clay ends up in the parking lot.
cloudy: Cloudy's good. Clay holds its moisture.
Nice gray day. Courts'll play true.
sunny: Hot sun bakes the clay. We'll need water later.
Beautiful day. Clay'll dry fast. Stay on it.

npcs.name: Coach Rafa Ibarra
npcs.bio: Head tennis pro from Valencia who played the satellite tour for six years and now teaches everyone from Lily to Mrs. Wellington.
quirks: Speaks in tennis proverbs
Draws footwork diagrams in the clay with his racket
Says 'vamos' to encourage, 'bueno' to disapprove
npcs.voice: Calm, unhurried, aphorisms and metaphors, the odd Spanish word, never raises his voice.

tennis.style: Heavy-topspin clay baseliner; never misses, never hurries

priya_sharma.note: His favorite project. 'Beautiful feet. The hands will come.'

theo_wellington.note: The most talented junior he's coached. Also the most sulky.

hank_morris.note: They disagree about clay watering with deep mutual respect.

jess_nakamura.note: She strings his rackets. He trusts her more than his own hands.

greetings: Ah, my friend. Vamos, another beautiful day.
Hola. You walk like you are late. You are not late. Breathe.
Good morning. The court is patient. So should we be.
Ey! The attendant. Tell me, how are your feet today?
Hola, hola. You have the look of a busy person. I respect busy.
requests: Could you bring a hopper of balls to Court 3 for my lesson?
The net on Court 4 is two centimetres low. I can see it. Hank says no.
Tell Theo his lesson is in ten minutes. He will pretend he did not hear.

satisfied: Vamos! Perfect footwork. I mean, perfect work.
Gracias. You have good timing. In life, it is everything.
Beautiful. Like a drop shot that dies.
unsatisfied: Bueno... it happens. The ball has no memory.
Hm. Next point is a new point.
Patience. Tennis is long, life is longer.
idle: The ball has no memory. Why should you?
Footwork first. Everything else is decoration.
Priya has the feet of a dancer. The racket, she holds like a spatula. We work on it.
Theo is fourteen and already hits like a man of thirty. He also sulks like a man of thirty.
Hank says the clay is too wet. I say it is too dry. We are both correct, in different ways.
In Valencia, we play on clay the color of paella. This is close. Very close.
Chad asks me for 'one secret' every week. The secret is practice. He does not like this secret.
morning: Morning lessons are the best. The mind is empty. Good for learning.
The first ball of the day, it tells you everything.
afternoon: Afternoon heat. Drink water. Drink more water.
My afternoon clinic has three children and one Bob. Bob is the hardest.
evening: Evening light is the most honest. You see the true spin.
After the lights, I string. It is my meditation.
rainy: Rain. We practice patience instead.
In the rain, the clay is heavy. Like my heart when a student forgets the split step.
windy: Wind is the best coach. It punishes the lazy toss.
Windy? Good. Now you learn to adjust.
cloudy: Cloudy. Good light for reading spin.
No shadows today. No excuses either.
sunny: Sun is good. But hats are better. Wear a hat.
Beautiful day. The clay is fast. Like me, twenty years ago.

npcs.name: Jess Nakamura
npcs.bio: Pro shop manager and master stringer who knows every member's string tension and racket history by heart.
quirks: Talks about members by their string tension
Alphabetises the grip tape
Deadpan to a fault; smiles once a season
npcs.voice: Deadpan, dry, precise numbers, short sentences, understatement.

tennis.style: Lefty slice artist who plays like she restrings: exactly

rafa_ibarra.note: Strings his rackets at 52 pounds, exactly, always.

chad_blake.note: Broken strings this season: 23. She keeps a chart.

kevin_park.note: Talked him out of a racket 'with a built-in sensor'. He's grateful.

gloria_castellano.note: The only person she'll restring a wooden racket for.

marcus_bell.note: Makes a joke about restringing hamstrings. She doesn't laugh at it either.

greetings: Hey. Welcome to the pro shop. Don't touch the grip display.
Oh. It's you. Good.
Hi. I've been awake since six. The stringing machine hasn't.
Hey. Chad broke another string. That's twenty-three.
Hello. Can I interest you in nothing? Good. Me neither.
requests: There's a racket on Court 1 that has been waiting for me since yesterday.

npcs.name: Dani Kowalski
npcs.bio: Head lifeguard and pool attendant. Former college distance swimmer who treats the pool deck like a small, sunny country with her as its border patrol.
quirks: Blows the whistle for emphasis, even mid-sentence
Wears white zinc on her nose from May to September
Counts everyone's laps, out loud, under her breath
npcs.voice: Bright, clipped, upbeat. Pool rules delivered like cheers. Lots of 'walking feet!' and counting.

tennis.style: Swims better than she volleys; returns everything with a smile

lily_santos.note: Teaches Lily's Saturday swim lessons. Best walking feet on the deck.

theo_wellington.note: Three cannonball warnings this summer. He thinks nobody saw. She saw.

harper_brandt.note: Harper books the pool for every party. Dani books a second lifeguard.

gus_papadakis.note: Trades five minutes of whistle duty for a grilled cheese. Fair deal.

otis_grant.note: He passes the pool fence every patrol. She counts him as backup.

greetings: Hi! Welcome to the deck! Walking feet, please. Thank you!
Hey! Sunscreen check: have you reapplied? Be honest.
Morning! Water's 26 degrees. I checked. Twice.
Hi hi! You're not here to cannonball, are you? Good.
Hey! Pool's open, chair's occupied, whistle's ready.
requests: The towel caddy's empty again. Could you grab a stack from the locker rooms?
If you see Theo heading this way with a running start, whistle for me.
Can you tell Gus I'll take my break in ten? He'll know what that means. Grilled cheese.

satisfied: Yes! That's a gold star. Real one, from my whistle drawer.
Perfect! You're a natural. Ever thought about lifeguarding?
Thank you! Deck's happy, I'm happy.
unsatisfied: Okay. Not ideal. Deep breaths. Pool breaths.
Hmm. That's a yellow flag. Not red. Yellow.
We'll call that a practice lap.
idle: Lily did a full length of backstroke yesterday. I may have cried behind my sunglasses.
Theo has cannonballed three times this summer. He thinks it's a secret. It is not a secret.
Harper's planning a flamingo pool party. I've already scheduled two extra guards and zero flamingos.
Gus makes the best grilled cheese in the county. I'd blow my whistle for it. I have.
Otis walks past the fence every hour on the dot. I set my water breaks by him.
Babs asked if the pool could be 'a bit less wet'. I said I'd look into it.
Rule one: walk. Rule two: no glass on the deck. Rule three: I see everything.
morning: Morning laps are the best laps. Nobody splashes before nine.
I tested the water at seven. Chlorine's perfect. You're welcome.
afternoon: Afternoon crowd! Juniors in the shallow end, grown-ups pretending to read.
Peak sun. Peak sunscreen. Reapply!
evening: Golden hour on the water. Best view at the club, honestly.
Last swims of the day. I'll start the 'five more minutes' countdown soon.
rainy: Rain means pool's closed. Thunder rule. I don't make the rules. Okay, I enforce them.
Everyone out! It's just rain, but rules are rules.
windy: Wind keeps blowing the towels into the pool. I'm fishing out laundry.
Umbrellas are down. They're sails today, not umbrellas.
cloudy: Cloudy! Still burn weather. UV doesn't care about clouds.
Gray sky, blue water. Nice contrast.
sunny: Sunny! Hydrate, reapply, repeat.
Perfect pool day. My chair's basically a throne today.
tips: Pro tip: the locker rooms keep the fresh towel stacks. The pool house keeps the dry ones. Don't mix them up in front of Frank.
If you need water fast, Gus's snack bar is right behind me. Faster than the café.
The pool gate's on the east side, off the perimeter path. Carts park on the path, not the deck. Please.
Lost sunglasses end up in the pool house lost-and-found. Lost kids end up with me. Both get returned.
hints: Looking for {name}? From my chair I spotted them {place}. I see everything.
Whistle report: {name} was {place} last I looked.
If you need {name}, they're {place}. I keep a mental map. Lifeguard brain.

npcs.name: Gus Papadakis
npcs.bio: Runs the pool house snack bar out of a hatch the size of a window. Thirty-one summers of grilled cheese, lemonade and everybody's business.
quirks: Remembers every member's order, and every member's secrets
Hums Greek folk songs over the fryer
Calls everyone 'boss', including the ducks
npcs.voice: Warm, rumbly, conspiratorial. Food metaphors, 'boss', and gossip delivered like a daily special.

tennis.style: Played once in 1994. Retired undefeated (one set, rain)

bob_hendricks.note: Two hot dogs for Bob. One hot dog, if Babs asks.

babs_hendricks.note: Gossip exchange at the hatch: she brings news, he brings fries.

hank_morris.note: Thirty years of 6 AM coffee together. About forty words exchanged. All good ones.

dani_kowalski.note: Covers her whistle breaks. Payment: she eats his grilled cheese and says 'wow'.

lily_santos.note: A free freeze-pop for every swim badge. She has eleven badges.

marcus_bell.note: Marcus tells members to skip the fries. Gus makes the fries better. It's a war.

greetings: Hey, boss! Hungry? You look hungry.
Boss! Just in time. Lemonade's fresh. Gossip's fresher.
Welcome to the finest hatch in the county. Also the only hatch.
Ah, my favorite attendant. Don't tell the others.
Hey, boss. Grill's hot, I'm hot, everybody's hot. Water?
requests: Babs ordered lemonade for her bridge club on the patio. Can you run it over? My legs are married to this hatch.
If Marcus asks, the fries are baked. They are not baked.
Tell Bob his hot dog is ready. Quietly.

satisfied: Boss! That's a five-star job. Six, with fries.
You're the real deal, boss. Freeze-pop's on me.
Beautiful. Like a grilled cheese, golden on both sides.
unsatisfied: Eh. Burnt toast, boss. It happens.
Not your best batch. We start fresh tomorrow.
Okay, okay. I've seen worse. I've cooked worse.
idle: Bob gets two hot dogs every Tuesday. If Babs asks, it's one hot dog and a salad. Understand, boss?
Marcus came by and asked for a 'kale option'. I gave him a pickle. It's green.
Lily has eleven swim badges. Eleven freeze-pops. I'm going broke and I love it.
Hank and me, thirty years of morning coffee. He said 'good coffee' in 2011. I still think about it.
Babs brings the news, I bring the fries. Best newspaper at the club.
Chad tried to pay with a signed ball. I took it. It's holding up the menu board.
Dani blows that whistle at the ducks. The ducks don't listen. Nobody tells ducks nothing.
morning: Morning, boss. Coffee's on. Grill's warming up. Me too.
Breakfast wraps till eleven. After that, you gotta know a guy. I'm the guy.
afternoon: Lunch rush! Six grilled cheese, four lemonades, one Frank asking for 'plain toast, dry'.
Afternoon, boss. Busiest hour. Also my favorite.
evening: Closing soon. Last call for fries. Don't tell Marcus.
Evening, boss. I'm scraping the grill. Very emotional time.
rainy: Rain! Everybody wants soup. I don't make soup. I'm making soup.
Pool's closed, hatch is open. Hot chocolate, boss?
windy: Wind keeps stealing my napkins. Club's got napkins in the trees now.
Hold onto your hat, boss. And your fries.
cloudy: Cloudy. Good grilled cheese weather. All weather is grilled cheese weather.
Gray day. Lemonade sales down, coffee up.
sunny: Sunny! Lemonade's flying out the hatch.
Hot one, boss. Take a water. On the house. Don't tell anybody.
tips: Tip from Gus: the pool house is the quickest place for water or towels on this side of the club. Everything else is a long walk.
Want to know what's going on at this club? Stand at my hatch for ten minutes. Everybody talks to the snack guy.
The café in the clubhouse does fancy coffee. I do real coffee. Both work, boss.
If a member's grumpy, bring them something cold. Nine times out of ten, that's the whole problem.
hints: {name}? Came by for a lemonade not long ago. Now they're {place}, I heard.
Word at the hatch says {name} is {place}. The hatch is never wrong, boss.
You want {name}? They're {place}. Tell 'em Gus says hi.

npcs.name: Marcus Bell
npcs.bio: Head trainer at the Fitness & Wellness centre. Ex-college sprinter with a clipboard, a stopwatch and boundless belief in everybody's hamstrings.
quirks: Counts reps in regular conversation
Calls everyone 'champ'
Carries a smoothie at all times; nobody has seen him buy one
npcs.voice: Hype-man energy, encouraging, reps and sets, 'champ', 'let's go'. Never negative, only 'not yet'.

tennis.style: Pure legs: gets to everything, hits it back with enthusiasm

nate_okafor.note: Spots Nate's squats and times his split-step. Nate logs both.

frank_deluca.note: Fifty push-ups at seventy-eight. Calls Marcus 'Sergeant'. Marcus has asked him not to.

leo_brandt.note: Pilot medical in six weeks. Leo does his cardio angry, which counts.

vik_rao.note: Vik prescribes rest. Marcus prescribes burpees. They agree on water.

gus_papadakis.note: Friendly war: kale smoothies versus Gus's fries. The fries are winning.

jess_nakamura.note: She restrings rackets, he restrings hamstrings. Her joke. She didn't laugh either.

greetings: Champ! Let's go! How are the legs today?
Hey hey! You walked in here. That's one rep. Proud of you.
Morning, champ! Hydrated? Stretched? Believing in yourself?
There they are! Rest day or leg day? Trick question. Leg day.
Champ! Perfect timing. I need somebody to high-five.
requests: I want to run a footwork boot camp. Could you borrow a ball hopper from the courts for me?
The cooler's running dry again. The spin crowd gets thirsty. Like, dramatic thirsty.
If you see Frank doing push-ups on the patio again, tell him: form first, champ.

satisfied: That's a personal best, champ! Let's go!
Crushed it! Up top!
Textbook form. I'm putting that on the whiteboard.
unsatisfied: Not yet, champ. Not yet is not never.
Okay, reset. Shake it out. We go again.
That's a warm-up set. The real set's coming.
idle: Frank did fifty push-ups this morning. He's seventy-eight. He called me 'Sergeant' after every ten.
Nate's split-step is 0.21 seconds. I timed it. He timed me timing it.
Leo's got a pilot medical in six weeks. He runs the treadmill like it owes him money.
Gus says fries are 'a potato-based recovery food'. I'm not saying he's right. I'm not saying he's wrong.
Vik keeps telling people to rest. I keep telling people to hydrate. Together we're one great doctor.
Somebody left a smoothie in the studio. It's been there since Monday. It's evolving.
Stretch before tennis, stretch after tennis, stretch while reading this sentence. Champ.
morning: Six AM class had eleven people. Eleven! Personal record.
Morning is for movement, champ. Coffee is for after.
afternoon: Afternoon slump? Ten squats. Right now. Kidding. Unless?
Midday crowd's the lunchtime spin class. Very intense. Very sweaty.
evening: Evening yoga at six. Bring a mat and your feelings.
Cool-down hours, champ. Stretch it out.
rainy: Rain means everybody's in here. Full house. I love it.
Rain day equals gym day. Nature's telling you to do lunges.
windy: Windy! Great resistance training for the walk over.
Wind sprints, but make it literal.
cloudy: Cloudy. Perfect outdoor run weather. Nobody overheats.
Gray sky, green light. Let's move.
sunny: Sunny! Hydrate, champ. Water first, then glory.
Beautiful out. Take the stairs. There are no stairs. Find some.
tips: Trainer tip: the fitness centre's by the north perimeter path, past the hard courts. The juice bar has the water cooler.
Members come back from matches thirsty. If you carry water toward the courts after a match, tips go up. Science.
Carrying heavy stuff? Take the cart. Lift with your legs, drive with your hands.
Frank's here at seven sharp, Nate at eight, Leo whenever he's angry. You can set a clock by 'em.
hints: Scouting report, champ: {name} is {place}. Go get 'em.
{name}? Saw them heading off. Should be {place}. Jog there. Good cardio.
{name} is {place}, champ. Go get 'em. That's your next rep.

npcs.name: Otis Grant
npcs.bio: Club security. Twenty-six years on the city force, then retired to a job with better lawns. Walks the perimeter every hour and knows every car, dog and gate latch on the property.
quirks: Knows every member by their license plate
Does the crossword on his breaks, in pen
Counts his steps: 22,000 is a slow day
npcs.voice: Calm, dry, unhurried. Speaks in short reports. Kind underneath, and occasionally very funny by accident.

tennis.style: Stands at the baseline like it's a post and returns everything, eventually

frank_deluca.note: Compare notes at the gate at seven sharp. Frank salutes. Otis nods.

hank_morris.note: Hank opens the shed, Otis opens the gate. Same thermos brand. Same opinions on geese.

chad_blake.note: Clocked Chad's car at 31 in a 10. Twice. Chad thinks they're buddies.

kevin_park.note: Unlocked Kevin's car three times. Kevin now wears his keys on a lanyard.

vik_rao.note: Keeps a spot open by the gate for when Dr. Rao's pager goes off.

dani_kowalski.note: Waves at the lifeguard chair every patrol. She whistles back. Twice means trouble.

greetings: Morning. Gate's open, lot's quiet. Good start.
Afternoon. Nothing to report. That's the best kind of report.
Hey there. You're on my list. The good list.
Evening. Seventeen thousand steps so far. Slow day.
Hello. Everything's secure. Except the crossword. Seven down is killing me.
requests: Found a racket by the perimeter fence. Dropped it at the locker room lost-and-found. Could you get it to the pro shop?
Somebody's parked across two spaces and the fire lane. I have a guess who.
If the pool gate's open after close, radio me. The raccoons are organized.

satisfied: Good work. I'll put it in the log. The good column.
Clean. Efficient. You'd have made a fine officer.
That's a closed case. Thank you.
unsatisfied: Hm. I'll note that. In pencil.
Not ideal. We learn, we move on.
That'll need a follow-up. Not today.
idle: Chad's car: silver, loud, fast. Clocked it at 31 in a 10. He waved at me. Twice.
I've unlocked Kevin's car three times. He wears his keys on a lanyard now. Growth.
Frank and I compare notes at seven sharp. Mostly about geese. The geese are a problem.
The raccoons tried the pool house bins again. They're getting smarter. So am I.
Dr. Rao gets the spot by the gate. When the pager goes, he's gone in ninety seconds. I've timed it.
Twenty-six years on the force. Now my biggest case is a missing visor. I like it better.
Seven down: 'Club where nothing happens, eleven letters'. I'm going with 'Greenbriar'. Doesn't fit. Still true.
morning: Opened the gate at six fifty-nine. Personal best.
Morning round done. Lot's quiet. Geese are not.
afternoon: Afternoon. Lot's full. Somebody always parks crooked.
Lunchtime is when people forget their headlights. I keep a list.
evening: Evening round. Checking every latch. Twice.
Lights coming on. I like the club at dusk. Quiet.
rainy: Rain. Everybody runs to their cars at once. Chaos. Organized chaos.
Wet patrol. Good boots. No complaints.
windy: Windy. The gate sign's swinging. I've got it.
Wind's knocking visors off heads. Lost-and-found's going to be full.
cloudy: Overcast. Easy on the eyes. Good patrol weather.
Clouds. No glare on the windshields. Plates read easy.
sunny: Sunny. Hot asphalt. Keep water in the cart.
Bright one. Sunglasses on, eyes open.
tips: Security tip: the perimeter path goes all the way around the club. With the cart, it's the fastest way from the gate to the clay courts.
Lost-and-found lives in the locker rooms. Rackets go to the pro shop after. Jess logs everything.
The pool gate is on the east side of the deck, right off the west perimeter path. Don't climb the fence. I will know.
If a member's missing, check the café first. Then the patio. Then the café again.
hints: Last patrol, I had {name} {place}. That's in the log.
{name}? Report says {place}. Give or take a few minutes.
You're looking for {name}. They're {place}. I don't guess, I observe.
